chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Jabbo's late arrivals and Cassino's food-titled tunes
summary: Jabbo showed up late to the gangsters' club, so Cassino Simpson took over; his tunes were all about soul food.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And I remember, he had to be living... Now, we were Downtown, at State and Lake Street, over there some place, and he was the South Side, down on 46th Street or 47th Street. My girlfriend lived there, a girl named Maud, and Jabbo lived in the apartment next door to her. Now, we were supposed to hit at 11 o'clock at night, and Jabbo was never there, and I'd have to call this girl and ask her if he could go over there and get him up. Now, of course, he wasn't going to go down to the job until about 12:30. Well, the gangsters got kind of tired of that. But he was playing so good, they just let it go.

So the next season, they just gave up on him and hired Cassino Simpson to be the leader, and then Jabbo went on some place else, and we stayed there with Cassino, and we finally played the Regal and got to make some pictures, and
then a (?) have some pictures made, and then made some appearances.

And Cassino was a nut. Everything he wrote, every tune he wrote had something about food. Pig feet and pig ears, mustard greens and pig knuckles... Every tune of his, black-eyed peas, red beans and rice... Every song we had, everything we had in the book was about that.
